A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the susceptibility to periodic breathing with pressure support during sleep is predictable and that the actual level is influenced by the difference between the eupneic PC02 and the PCO2 apnea threshold as well as the respiratory rate response to pressure support.

the development of periodic breathing during assisted ventilation during sleep is predictable and is influenced by the product of spontaneous minute ventilation and elastance, DeltaPCO2, and DeltaRR, but not by the Pmus response to pressure support.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the development of periodic breathing during assisted ventilation with either PSV or PAV is entirely predictable during normal sleep, and that this phenomenon is due to the existence of a PCO2 threshold for central apnea during sleep.
